title: AI-Based System for Monitoring Knee Movement During Rehabilitation
content: Knee joint injuries and post-surgical rehabilitation require accurate, continuous monitoring of the joint’s range of motion (ROM) to ensure effective recovery and prevent long-term complications. Traditional assessment methods rely on intermittent, manual measurements performed during clinical visits, which lack consistency, objectivity, and real-time feedback.  This work focuses on the specification, design, development, and proof-of-concept (POC) implementation of an AI-enhanced wearable monitoring system for knee rehabilitation. The system is based on a dual-sensor architecture positioned on the T-Scope brace. The system captures synchronized motion data from both sensors and computes the relative angle between them in order to derive the real-time range of motion (ROM) of the knee.  The proposed system demonstrates a complete end-to-end pipeline, from sensor-level data acquisition to cloud-based storage and AI-driven analysis. The proof-of-concept implementation indicates that the system can serve as a reliable, low-cost, and scalable solution for home-based rehabilitation monitoring. By providing continuous, objective, and data-driven feedback, the system has the potential to improve rehabilitation outcomes and enhance patient adherence to prescribed therapy protocols.
